panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Cardiac MRI in a real patient with Williams-Beuren syndrome shows turbulent systolic flow above the aortic valve, consistent with supravalvular aortic stenosis. B: Phase-contrast cardiac MRI in the same patient shows abnormal crescent-like aortic flow at the sinotubular junction, supporting supravalvular aortic stenosis in Williams-Beuren syndrome. C: Cardiac CTA demonstrates a supravalvular aortic membrane and hourglass stenosis of the proximal ascending aorta, a classic manifestation of Williams-Beuren syndrome. D: Cardiac CTA volume rendering shows hourglass proximal ascending aortic stenosis and mild supravalvular pulmonary stenosis, both known cardiovascular manifestations of Williams-Beuren syndrome.

panels.figure_caption: Multimodality imaging assessment of supravalvular aortic stenosis in a 37-year-old man.
